seo.metaTitle: Grayscale PNG Converter - Free, No Upload
seo.metaDescription: Turn a PNG into shades of gray with the standard BT.601 luminance formula. Transparency is preserved. Free, no upload, no settings, runs in your browser.
seo.longDescription: Convert PNG to grayscale replaces every color with a shade of gray, computed with the standard BT.601 luminance formula that matches human brightness perception — a red pixel becomes the same gray a camera would render, not a flat average of its channels. Transparency is left untouched, so a logo keeps its clean edges instead of gaining a gray box. There are no settings to tune: upload, read the result, download — and the whole thing happens in your browser, with your file never leaving the device.
facts: Runs entirely in your browser: no upload, no server, no signup.
Standard BT.601 luminance formula — the same gray a camera would render.
Alpha is untouched: a transparent PNG stays transparent.
Per-pixel calculation, no compression — save as PNG or WebP to keep it lossless.
Free with no daily limit, no watermark and no account, also for commercial use.
howTo: Drop the image into the source area, or pick a file from your device.
Read the preview: the colors are already replaced by shades of gray.
Save the result as PNG, JPG, WebP or BMP from the Download button.

faq.q: What is the difference between grayscale and black and white?
faq.a: Grayscale keeps a continuous range of grays, so the image still looks like the original - just without color. Black and white reduces everything to exactly two values with a sharp threshold, which flattens photos. If you need the two-value version, run the black-and-white tool afterwards.
Yes. Only the color channels are converted; the alpha channel is copied as it is, so a transparent PNG stays transparent and the edges of a cut-out logo stay clean.

Within the tool, yes: it is a per-pixel channel calculation, not a compression, so no detail is thrown away. The output format still matters - save as PNG or WebP to keep it lossless, and remember JPG has no transparency.

faq.q: Are my images uploaded to convert them?
faq.a: No. The conversion runs in your browser tab, with no upload, no account, no daily limit and no watermark. The tool is free for commercial use and open source.
